state.case_summary:
A primigravid patient in their 20s during the eighth month of gestation presented with history of regular nonexertional episodic palpitations that lasted for a few minutes and subsided spontaneously over the past several days. The patient had no associated sweating, syncope, dyspnoea, orthopnoea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea. Visible neck pulsation was noticed by the patient's mother. The patient had no chronic medical comorbid conditions and was not taking any medications.

Blood pressure was 110/70 mm Hg and heart rate was 120 beats/min. The general examination was unremarkable. The jugular venous pulsations revealed regular cannon waves, and auscultation was significant for a variable first heart sound. Examination findings of other systems were normal.

- Laboratory tests: Complete blood cell count, kidney function, liver function, thyroid function, serum electrolytes, and cardiac troponin were within normal limits.- Imaging/Other tests:   - 2-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography showed good biventricular function and normally functioning valves    - ECG findings:    Image Title: ECG taken at admission    Image Description: Regular narrow QRS tachycardia (QRS duration, 60 milliseconds) at a ventricular rate of 103-125 beats/min with mean cycle length of 509.16 milliseconds, QRS axis of +60°, and QTc of 404 milliseconds. Regular P waves evident marching onto QRS complexes at a rate of 100-125 beats/min with mean cycle length of 517.16 milliseconds with varying PR intervals.

root.label: Palpitations of Uncertain Aetiology with Regular Narrow QRS Tachycardia
